To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) MM-based orthotropic material properties can be used to accurately predict the strain and displacement response in the femur under a simple stance position loading condition, (ii) the MM-based orthotropic properties match empirically based isotropy, and (iii) both match the experimental data well.
the use of orthotropic material properties, determined by MM-based approach, is a valid approach in FE analyses of femurs.
The use of patient-specific high-order FE models based on QCT and orthotropic material properties can accurately predict strains in the femur under simple stance position loading.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the generation of high order patient-specific FE models of human femur based on quantitative computer-tomography with inhomogeneous MM based orthotropic and isotropically properties, and with the experimental validation of the FE models.
the development of high-order FE models of femurs with orthotropic properties and the validation of the FE results with in vitro experiments.
the development of high order finite element (FE) models for human femurs based upon QCT data, with inhomogeneous and orthotropic material properties.

the MM-based orthotropic properties are as accurate as the isotropic properties in the prediction of strains and displacements in the femur.

the MM-based orthotropic properties can be used to generate high-fidelity FE models of the femur that match well with the empirically based isotropically properties and experimental results.

the use of MM-based orthotropic properties is a valid approach in the FEA of femur bones, and that the use of inhomogeneous material properties in the FEA is important for the prediction of strains in the femur head and neck.

the MM-based orthotropic properties are as good as the isotropic material properties in terms of their ability to capture the femur's response to a simple stance position loading.
orthotropic properties can be used in FE models of femurs, with the caveat that the orthotropic properties should not be determined from the FE model itself.
